messages:
ravi: Hey team, new hire hitting multiple redwoodctl pains on WSL2. Installer left config unreadable and local-test keeps recycling auth tokens + my app port 8080 collides with runtime so the test runtime dies silently. Need quick fixes for onboarding.

ravi: Steps: Windows 11 + WSL2 (Ubuntu 22.04), `scoop install redwoodctl` then `redwoodctl init --profile dev-ravi` then `redwoodctl local-test --port 8080 --mount ./seed:/app/seed --debug`. redwoodctl v0.30.1.

emma: Oof. What do logs say? paste a short snippet.

ravi: snippet: 
```
WARN installer: wrote config with mode 0600 to /home/ravi/.redwood/config but owner uid 0
ERROR runtime: failed to bind port 8080: address already in use
INFO auth: refresh attempt 1 -> 401; refresh attempt 2 -> 401; falling back to interactive code (waiting)
```
The interactive wait blocks my WSL terminal and our CI runner (self-hosted).

liam: Two separate things: installer file ownership and auth fallback + port collision. For WSL ownership sometimes Windows process (uid 0 shim) writes the file; `chown $(id -u):$(id -g) ~/.redwood/config` fixes it. We'll push an atomic-write+chown fix but quick workaround is to run `redwoodctl repair-profile` after install.

emma: For port collisions we should detect bind errors earlier and surface a clear message. Does `--port` map host->guest or is it a runtime port only?

ravi: It maps host port into the runtime. I had a local dev server already on 8080 and redwoodctl tried to attach to same host port. No friendly error was shown, it just exits and local-test stays in a restart loop.

liam: We'll add an explicit preflight that checks the requested ports before spinning up the runtime and fail fast with exit code 2 and suggestion to choose a different port (or auto-find free port with a --ephemeral flag).

emma: About auth: redwoodctl keeps attempting refresh and when it gets 401 it starts the interactive browser flow. In noninteractive shells (CI or WSL headless) that blocks. We should expose `REDWOOD_AUTH_MODE=noninteractive|interactive|prompt` and if noninteractive then return a 78 exit code and a short message describing how to provide a token via `REDWOOD_TOKEN` or service account key.

ravi: Workaround I used in CI: `redwoodctl auth login --service-account-key "$SA_KEY" --output token > /tmp/rw_token && export REDWOOD_TOKEN=$(cat /tmp/rw_token)` then run local-test. That prevented the interactive fallback but I still hit the port issue which made the job restart forever.

devx-bot: Note: internal infra issue #4120 tracks atomic installer writes on WSL + chown; issue #4121 tracks preflight port checks; issue #4122 tracks REDWOOD_AUTH_MODE env.

liam: I'll pick up #4121 and #4122. Short-term we can add a check in the CLI that detects interactive capability: if `tty` is missing or `CI` env is set, and refresh fails, error out instead of waiting. Also we'll log a one-line actionable message so CI doesn't hang.

ravi: Created a tiny gist with minimal repro and job logs: https://gist.github.com/ravi/4d5f9e. Also added a CI job snippet that worked for me: 
```
- run: redwoodctl auth login --service-account-key "$SA_KEY" --output token > /tmp/rw_token
- run: echo "REDWOOD_TOKEN=$(cat /tmp/rw_token)" >> $GITHUB_ENV
- run: redwoodctl local-test --port 9090 --mount $(pwd)/seed:/app/seed --debug
```
Using port 9090 avoided the collision.

emma: Thanks. Followups: 1) infra-eng add atomic installer write+chown; 2) CLI preflight for ports + --ephemeral option; 3) add REDWOOD_AUTH_MODE and noninteractive error path; 4) update onboarding docs with quick CI token snippet and WSL chown workaround.

infra-eng: Acknowledged, will prioritize installer fix (high) and CLI auth mode (medium). If anyone hits this while onboarding ping infra and we'll provide a temporary token. :handshake:
